    14→Role = Literal[
    15→    "system",  # Origin is system prompt
    16→    "user",  # Origin is user
    17→    "assistant",  # Origin is the model output
    18→    "ipython",  # Origin is return from a tool call
    19→]
    20→

    22→class Message:
    23→    """
    24→    This class represents individual messages in a fine-tuning dataset. It supports
    25→    text-only content, text with interleaved images, and tool calls. The :class:`~torchtune.modules.tokenizers.ModelTokenizer`
    26→    will tokenize the content of the message using ``tokenize_messages`` and attach
    27→    the appropriate special tokens based on the flags set in this class.
    28→
    29→    Args:
    30→        role (Role): role of the message writer. Can be "system" for system prompts,
    31→            "user" for human prompts, "assistant" for model responses, or "ipython"
    32→            for tool call returns.
    33→        content (Union[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]]): content of the message. If it is text only content,
    34→            you can pass in a string. If it is multimodal content, pass in a list of dictionaries formatted
    35→            as follows::
    36→
    37→                [
    38→                    {"type": "image", "content": <PIL.Image.Image>},
    39→                    {"type": "text", "content": "What is in this image?"},
    40→                ]
    41→
    42→        masked (bool): whether the message is masked in the sample. If True, do not use
    43→            in loss calculation. Default: False
    44→        ipython (bool): whether the message is a tool call. Default: False
    45→        eot (bool): whether the message corresponds to the end of a turn, where control is handed over
    46→            to the assistant from the user or the user from the assistant. Default: True. Should be true
    47→            in most cases except for:
    48→
    49→            - For multiple consecutive assistant messages (i.e., tool calls
    50→              by assistant), only the last assistant message will have ``eot=True``
    51→            - All ipython messages (tool call returns) should set ``eot=False``.
    52→
    53→    Note:
    54→        Message class expects any image content to be in
    55→        `PIL Image format <https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/Image.html#PIL.Image.Image>`_.
    56→    """
    57→
    58→    def __init__(
    59→        self,
    60→        role: Role,
    61→        content: Union[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]],
    62→        masked: bool = False,
    63→        ipython: bool = False,
    64→        eot: bool = True,
    65→    ):
    66→        self.role = role
    67→        self.content = self._convert_to_list_of_dict(content)
    68→        self.masked = masked
    69→        self.ipython = ipython
    70→        self.eot = eot
    71→
    72→        self._validate_message()
    73→
    74→    def _convert_to_list_of_dict(self, content) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    75→        """User is currently allowed to pass in a string for text-only content.
    76→        This ensures that the content is formatted as a list of dictionaries."""
    77→        if isinstance(content, str):
    78→            return [{"type": "text", "content": content}]
    79→
    80→        assert isinstance(
    81→            content, list
    82→        ), f"content must be of type List[Dict[str, Any]], got {content}"
    83→
    84→        return content
    85→
    86→    @classmethod
    87→    def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> "Message":
    88→        """
    89→        Construct a Message from a dictionary.
    90→
    91→        Args:
    92→            d (dict): dictionary containing the fields of the Message.
    93→
    94→        Returns:
    95→            Message: constructed Message.
    96→        """
    97→        return cls(
    98→            role=d["role"],
    99→            content=d["content"],
   100→            masked=d.get("masked", False),
   101→            ipython=d.get("ipython", False),
   102→            eot=d.get("eot", True),
   103→        )
   104→
   105→    def get_media(self) -> List["PIL.Image.Image"]:
   106→        """
   107→        Returns media content of the message.
   108→        """
   109→        return [
   110→            content["content"] for content in self.content if content["type"] == "image"
   111→        ]
   112→
   113→    @property
   114→    def contains_media(self) -> bool:
   115→        """
   116→        Returns whether the message contains media.
   117→        """
   118→        return any(content["type"] == "image" for content in self.content)
   119→
   120→    @property
   121→    def text_content(self) -> str:
   122→        """
   123→        Returns text-only content of the message.
   124→        """
   125→        return "".join(
   126→            content["content"] for content in self.content if content["type"] == "text"
   127→        )
   128→
   129→    def _validate_message(self) -> None:
   130→        if self.ipython and self.contains_media:
   131→            raise ValueError(
   132→                f"Media tokens in tool calls are not supported. Both are set in message: {self.text_content}"
   133→            )
   134→        if self.ipython and self.role != "assistant":
   135→            raise ValueError(
   136→                f"Only assistant messages can be tool calls. Found role {self.role} in message: {self.text_content}"
   137→            )
   138→
   139→    def __repr__(self) -> str:
   140→        content_only = [content["content"] for content in self.content]
   141→        return f"Message(role='{self.role}', content={content_only!r})"
   142→

   144→class InputOutputToMessages(Transform):
   145→    """
   146→    Message transform class that converts a single sample with "input" and "output" fields,
   147→    (or equivalent fields specified in column_map) to user and assistant messages,
   148→    respectively. This is useful for datasets that have two columns, one containing
   149→    the user prompt string and the other containing the model response string::
   150→
   151→        |  input          |  output          |
   152→        |-----------------|------------------|
   153→        | "user prompt"   | "model response" |
   154→
   155→    Args:
   156→        train_on_input (bool): Whether the model is trained on the user prompt or not.
   157→            Default is False.
   158→        column_map (Optional[Dict[str, str]]): a mapping to change the expected "input"
   159→            and "output" column names to the actual column names in the dataset. Keys should
   160→            be "input" and "output" and values should be the actual column names. Default is None,
   161→            keeping the default "input" and "output" column names.
   162→        new_system_prompt (Optional[str]): if specified, prepend a system message. This can
   163→            serve as instructions to guide the model response. Default is None.
   164→        image_dir (Optional[Path]): path to the directory containing the images that is prepended to all image
   165→            paths in the dataset. For example, if ``image_dir="/home/user/dataset/"` and the sample image path
   166→            was ``"images/1.jpg"``, the final image path that will be loaded is ``"/home/user/dataset/images/1.jpg"``.
   167→            If None, assume images are available in current working directory or are located
   168→            on a remote url. For text-only, leave as None. Default is None.
   169→
   170→    Raises:
   171→        ValueError: If ``column_map`` is provided and ``input`` not in ``column_map``, or
   172→            ``output`` not in ``column_map``.
   173→    """
   174→
   175→    def __init__(
   176→        self,
   177→        train_on_input: bool = False,
   178→        column_map: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
   179→        new_system_prompt: Optional[str] = None,
   180→        image_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
   181→    ):
   182→        self.train_on_input = train_on_input
   183→        self.new_system_prompt = new_system_prompt
   184→
   185→        self.column_map = column_map
   186→
   187→        if self.column_map is not None:
   188→            if "input" not in self.column_map:
   189→                raise ValueError(
   190→                    f"Expected a key of 'input' in column_map but found {self.column_map.keys()}."
   191→                )
   192→            if "output" not in self.column_map:
   193→                raise ValueError(
   194→                    f"Expected a key of 'output' in column_map but found {self.column_map.keys()}."
   195→                )
   196→        else:
   197→            self.column_map = {"input": "input", "output": "output", "image": "image"}
   198→
   199→        self.image_dir = image_dir
   200→
   201→    def __call__(self, sample: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
   202→        is_multimodal = "image" in sample or (
   203→            "image" in self.column_map and self.column_map["image"] in sample
   204→        )
   205→
   206→        if is_multimodal:
   207→            image_path = sample[self.column_map["image"]]
   208→            if isinstance(image_path, str):
   209→                if self.image_dir is not None:
   210→                    image_path = self.image_dir / image_path
   211→                # Load if not loaded
   212→                pil_image = load_image(image_path)
   213→            else:
   214→                pil_image = image_path
   215→            content = [
   216→                {"type": "image", "content": pil_image},
   217→                {"type": "text", "content": sample[self.column_map["input"]]},
   218→            ]
   219→        else:
   220→            content = [{"type": "text", "content": sample[self.column_map["input"]]}]
   221→
   222→        output_content = [
   223→            {"type": "text", "content": sample[self.column_map["output"]]}
   224→        ]
   225→
   226→        messages = [
   227→            Message(
   228→                role="user",
   229→                content=content,
   230→                masked=not self.train_on_input,
   231→                eot=True,
   232→            ),
   233→            Message(
   234→                role="assistant",
   235→                content=output_content,
   236→                masked=False,
   237→                eot=True,
   238→            ),
   239→        ]
   240→        if self.new_system_prompt is not None:
   241→            messages = [
   242→                Message(
   243→                    role="system", content=self.new_system_prompt, masked=True, eot=True
   244→                )
   245→            ] + messages
   246→        return {"messages": messages}

   249→class ChosenRejectedToMessages(Transform):
   250→    """
   251→    Transform for converting a single sample from datasets with "chosen" and "rejected" columns
   252→    containing conversations to a list of chosen and rejected messages. For example::
   253→
   254→        |  chosen                                |  rejected                              |
   255→        |----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
   256→        | [{"role": "user", "content": Q1},      | [{"role": "user", "content": Q1},      |
   257→        |  {"role": "assistant", "content": A1}] |  {"role": "assistant", "content": A2}] |
   258→
   259→    will be converted to:
   260→
   261→    .. code-block:: python
   262→
   263→        chosen = [
   264→            Message(role="user", content="Q1"),
   265→            Message(role="assistant", content="A1"),
   266→        ]
   267→        rejected = [
   268→            Message(role="user", content="Q1"),
   269→            Message(role="assistant", content="A2"),
   270→        ]
   271→
   272→    A single sample typically consists of a single optional system prompt and one or multiple
   273→    turns of user and assistant messages.
   274→
   275→    Args:
   276→        train_on_input (bool): Whether the model is trained on the user prompt or not.
   277→            Default is False.
   278→        column_map (Optional[Dict[str, str]]): a mapping to change the expected
   279→            "chosen" and "rejected" column names to the actual column names in the dataset.
   280→            Keys should be "chosen" and "rejected" and values should be the actual column names.
   281→            Default is None, keeping the default column names.
   282→        new_system_prompt (Optional[str]): if specified, prepend a system message. This can
   283→            serve as instructions to guide the model response. Setting this will OVERRIDE any system
   284→            messages already present in the dataset. Default is None.
   285→
   286→    Raises:
   287→        ValueError: If ``column_map`` is provided and ``chosen`` not in ``column_map``, or
   288→            ``rejected`` not in ``column_map``.
   289→    """
   290→
   291→    def __init__(
   292→        self,
   293→        train_on_input: bool = False,
   294→        column_map: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
   295→        new_system_prompt: Optional[str] = None,
   296→    ):
   297→        self.train_on_input = train_on_input
   298→        self.new_system_prompt = new_system_prompt
   299→        if column_map:
   300→            if "chosen" not in column_map:
   301→                raise ValueError(
   302→                    f"Expected a key of 'chosen' in column_map but found {column_map.keys()}."
   303→                )
   304→            if "rejected" not in column_map:
   305→                raise ValueError(
   306→                    f"Expected a key of 'rejected' in column_map but found {column_map.keys()}."
   307→                )
   308→            self._column_map = column_map
   309→        else:
   310→            self._column_map = {"chosen": "chosen", "rejected": "rejected"}
   311→
   312→    def __call__(self, sample: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
   313→        chosen_messages = []
   314→        for message in sample[self._column_map["chosen"]]:
   315→            if message["role"] == "system" and self.new_system_prompt is not None:
   316→                continue
   317→            message["masked"] = (message["role"] != "assistant") and (
   318→                not self.train_on_input
   319→            )
   320→            chosen_messages.append(Message.from_dict(message))
   321→
   322→        rejected_messages = []
   323→        for message in sample[self._column_map["rejected"]]:
   324→            if message["role"] == "system" and self.new_system_prompt is not None:
   325→                continue
   326→            message["masked"] = (message["role"] != "assistant") and (
   327→                not self.train_on_input
   328→            )
   329→            rejected_messages.append(Message.from_dict(message))
   330→
   331→        if self.new_system_prompt is not None:
   332→            chosen_messages = [
   333→                Message(
   334→                    role="system", content=self.new_system_prompt, masked=True, eot=True
   335→                )
   336→            ] + chosen_messages
   337→            rejected_messages = [
   338→                Message(
   339→                    role="system", content=self.new_system_prompt, masked=True, eot=True
   340→                )
   341→            ] + rejected_messages
   342→
   343→        return {"chosen": chosen_messages, "rejected": rejected_messages}

   346→class ShareGPTToMessages(Transform):
   347→    """
   348→    Convert a single chat sample adhering to the ShareGPT JSON structure to torchtune's :class:`~torchtune.data.Message`
   349→    structure.
   350→
   351→    A single sample typically consists of a single optional system prompt and one or multiple
   352→    turns of user and assistant messages.
   353→
   354→    ShareGPT follows::
   355→
   356→        {
   357→            "conversations": [
   358→                {
   359→                    "from": <system|human|gpt>,
   360→                    "value": <message>,
   361→                },
   362→                ...
   363→            ]
   364→        }
   365→
   366→    :class:`~torchtune.data.Message` follows::
   367→
   368→        [
   369→            {
   370→                "role": <system|user|assistant>,
   371→                "content": <message>,
   372→            },
   373→            ...
   374→        ]
   375→
   376→    Args:
   377→        train_on_input (bool): whether the prompt should remain unmasked. For multimodal datasets, ``train_on_input``
   378→            is always False and this value is ignored. Default: False
   379→        column_map (Optional[Dict[str, str]]): a mapping from the expected columns ("conversations")
   380→            to the new column names in the dataset. Key should be "conversations" and value should
   381→            be the new column name. If None, keep the default "conversations".
   382→            Default is None.
   383→        new_system_prompt (Optional[str]): if specified, prepend a system message. This can
   384→            serve as instructions to guide the model response. Setting this will OVERRIDE any system
   385→            messages already present in the dataset. Default is None.
   386→        image_dir (Optional[Path]): path to the directory containing the images that is prepended to all image
   387→            paths in the dataset. For example, if ``image_dir="/home/user/dataset/"` and the sample image path
   388→            was ``"images/1.jpg"``, the final image path that will be loaded is ``"/home/user/dataset/images/1.jpg"``.
   389→            If None, assume images are available in current working directory or are located
   390→            on a remote url. For text-only, leave as None. Default is None.
   391→        image_tag (Optional[str]): placeholder tags in the text content of each message to be replaced by image
   392→            special tokens. If images are present and this is None, then will prepend image tokens to the first
   393→            user message in the sample by default. If text-only, this field is ignored. Default is ``"<image>"``.
   394→
   395→    Raises:
   396→        ValueError: If ``column_map`` is provided and ``conversations`` not in ``column_map``.
   397→    """
   398→
   399→    def __init__(
   400→        self,
   401→        train_on_input: bool = False,
   402→        column_map: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
   403→        new_system_prompt: Optional[str] = None,
   404→        image_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
   405→        image_tag: Optional[str] = "<image>",
   406→    ):
   407→        self.train_on_input = train_on_input
   408→        self.new_system_prompt = new_system_prompt
   409→        if column_map:
   410→            if "conversations" not in column_map:
   411→                raise ValueError(
   412→                    f"Expected a key of 'conversations' in column_map but found {column_map.keys()}."
   413→                )
   414→            self._column_map = column_map
   415→        else:
   416→            self._column_map = {"conversations": "conversations", "image": "image"}
   417→        self.image_dir = image_dir
   418→        self.image_tag = image_tag
   419→
   420→    def __call__(self, sample: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
   421→        """
   422→        Return a list of Message objects from the provided sample dict.
   423→
   424→        Args:
   425→            sample (Mapping[str, Any]): a single data sample with "messages" field pointing
   426→                to a list of dict messages.
   427→
   428→        Returns:
   429→            List[Message]: A list of messages with "role" and "content" fields.
   430→        """
   431→        role_map = {"system": "system", "human": "user", "gpt": "assistant"}
   432→        messages = []
   433→        if self.new_system_prompt is not None:
   434→            messages.append(
   435→                Message(
   436→                    role="system", content=self.new_system_prompt, masked=True, eot=True
   437→                )
   438→            )
   439→
   440→        is_multimodal = "image" in sample or (
   441→            "image" in self._column_map and self._column_map["image"] in sample
   442→        )
   443→
   444→        # Gate variable to ensure that we only prepend image tokens to the first user message
   445→        image_loaded = False
   446→        for message in sample[self._column_map["conversations"]]:
   447→            role = role_map[message["from"]]
   448→            content = message["value"]
   449→            if role == "system" and self.new_system_prompt is not None:
   450→                continue
   451→            if role == "user":
   452→                if is_multimodal and not image_loaded:
   453→                    image_path = sample[self._column_map["image"]]
   454→                    if self.image_dir is not None:
   455→                        image_path = self.image_dir / image_path
   456→                    pil_image = load_image(image_path)
   457→                    # If image tag is not specified, prepend by default
   458→                    if self.image_tag is None:
   459→                        content = [
   460→                            {"type": "image", "content": pil_image},
   461→                            {"type": "text", "content": content},
   462→                        ]
   463→                    else:
   464→                        content = format_content_with_images(
   465→                            content,
   466→                            image_tag=self.image_tag,
   467→                            images=[pil_image],
   468→                        )
   469→                    image_loaded = True
   470→
   471→            # If multimodal and user message, always mask
   472→            # Otherwise, if user message, mask if train_on_input is False
   473→            masked = (role != "assistant") and (
   474→                not self.train_on_input or is_multimodal
   475→            )
   476→            messages.append(Message(role=role, content=content, masked=masked))
   477→
   478→        return {"messages": messages}

   481→class OpenAIToMessages(Transform):
   482→    """
   483→    Convert a single chat sample adhering to the `OpenAI chat completion <https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat>`_
   484→    JSON structure to torchtune's :class:`~torchtune.data.Message` structure. This supports both
   485→    text and image messages.
   486→
   487→    A single sample typically consists of a single optional system prompt and one or multiple
   488→    turns of user and assistant messages.
   489→
   490→    For example::
   491→
   492→        {
   493→            "messages": [
   494→                {
   495→                    "role": <system|user|assistant>,
   496→                    "content": [
   497→                        {
   498→                            "type": "text",
   499→                            "text": "What'\''s in this image?",
   500→                        },
   501→                        {
   502→                            "type": "image_url",
   503→                            "image_url": {
   504→                                "url": <url>,
   505→                            },
   506→                        },
   507→                },
   508→                ...
   509→            ]
   510→        }
   511→
   512→    :class:`~torchtune.data.Message` follows::
   513→
   514→        [
   515→            {
   516→                "role": <system|user|assistant>,
   517→                "content": [
   518→                    {
   519→                        "type": "text",
   520→                        "content": "What'\''s in this image?",
   521→                    },
   522→                    {
   523→                        "type": "image",
   524→                        "content": <PIL.Image.Image>,
   525→                    },
   526→                ],
   527→            },
   528→            ...
   529→        ]
   530→
   531→    Args:
   532→        train_on_input (bool): whether the prompt should remain unmasked. Default: False
   533→        column_map (Optional[Dict[str, str]]): a mapping from the expected columns ("messages")
   534→            to the new column names in the dataset. Key should be "messages" and value should be
   535→            the new column name. If None, keep the default "messages".
   536→            Default is None.
   537→        new_system_prompt (Optional[str]): if specified, prepend a system message. This can
   538→            serve as instructions to guide the model response. Setting this will OVERRIDE any system
   539→            messages already present in the dataset. Default is None.
   540→
   541→    Raises:
   542→        ValueError: If ``column_map`` is provided and ``messages`` not in ``column_map``.
   543→    """
   544→
   545→    def __init__(
   546→        self,
   547→        train_on_input: bool = False,
   548→        column_map: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
   549→        new_system_prompt: Optional[str] = None,
   550→    ):
   551→        self.train_on_input = train_on_input
   552→        self.new_system_prompt = new_system_prompt
   553→        if column_map:
   554→            if "messages" not in column_map:
   555→                raise ValueError(
   556→                    f"Expected a key of 'messages' in column_map but found {column_map.keys()}."
   557→                )
   558→            self._column_map = column_map
   559→        else:
   560→            self._column_map = {"messages": "messages"}
   561→
   562→    def _convert_from_openai_content(
   563→        self, content: List[Dict[str, Any]]
   564→    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   565→        """Converts a list of content dicts from the OpenAI format to the torchtune format."""
   566→        converted_content = []
   567→        for content_dict in content:
   568→            if content_dict["type"] == "text":
   569→                converted_content.append(
   570→                    {"type": "text", "content": content_dict["text"]}
   571→                )
   572→            elif content_dict["type"] == "image_url":
   573→                converted_content.append(

   585→        Args:

   618→def validate_messages(
   619→    messages: List[Message],
   620→) -> None:
   621→    """
   622→    Given a list of messages, ensure that messages form a valid
   623→    back-and-forth conversation. An error will be raised if:
   624→
   625→    - There is a system message that's not the first message
   626→    - There are two consecutive user messages
   627→    - An assistant message comes before the first user message
   628→    - The message is empty
   629→    - Messages are shorter than length of 2 (min. one user-assistant turn)
   630→
   631→
   632→    Args:
   633→        messages (List[Message]): the messages to validate.
   634→
   635→    Raises:
   636→        ValueError: If the messages are invalid.
   637→    """
   638→    if len(messages) < 2:
   639→        raise ValueError(
   640→            f"Messages must be at least length 2, but got {len(messages)} messages"
   641→        )
   642→
   643→    last_turn = "assistant"
   644→    for i, message in enumerate(messages):
   645→        if message.role == "assistant" and last_turn != "user":
   646→            raise ValueError(
   647→                f"Assistant message before expected user message at index {i} in messages"
   648→            )
   649→        if message.role == "user" and last_turn == "user":
   650→            raise ValueError(
   651→                f"Two consecutive user messages at index {i} and {i - 1} in messages"
   652→            )
   653→        if message.role == "system" and i > 0:
   654→            raise ValueError(
   655→                f"System message at index {i} in messages, but system messages must come first"
   656→            )
   657→        last_turn = message.role

   660→class AlpacaToMessages(Transform):
   661→    """
   662→    Message transform class for Alpaca-style datasets with "instruction", "input", and "output"
   663→    (or equivalent fields specified in column_map) columns. User messages are formed from the
   664→    instruction + input columns and assistant messages are formed from the output column. Prompt
   665→    templating is conditional on the presence of the "input" column, and thus is handled directly
   666→    in this transform class instead of a dedicated :class:`~torchtune.data.PromptTemplate` class
   667→    due to this custom logic.
   668→
   669→    Args:
   670→        train_on_input (bool): Whether the model is trained on the user prompt or not.
   671→            Default is True.
   672→        column_map (Optional[Dict[str, str]]): a mapping to change the expected "instruction", "input",
   673→            and "output" column names to the actual column names in the dataset. Default is None,
   674→            keeping the default column names.
   675→    """
   676→
   677→    def __init__(
   678→        self, train_on_input: bool = True, column_map: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None
   679→    ):
   680→        self.train_on_input = train_on_input
   681→        self.column_map = column_map
   682→        self.template = {
   683→            "prompt_input": (
   684→                "Below is an instruction that describes a task, paired with an input that provides further context. "
   685→                "Write a response that appropriately completes the request.\n\n"
   686→                "### Instruction:\n{instruction}\n\n### Input:\n{input}\n\n### Response:\n"
   687→            ),
   688→            "prompt_no_input": (
   689→                "Below is an instruction that describes a task. "
   690→                "Write a response that appropriately completes the request.\n\n"
   691→                "### Instruction:\n{instruction}\n\n### Response:\n"
   692→            ),
   693→        }
   694→
   695→    def __call__(self, sample: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
   696→        column_map = self.column_map or {}
   697→        key_input = column_map.get("input", "input")
   698→        key_instruction = column_map.get("instruction", "instruction")
   699→        key_output = column_map.get("output", "output")
   700→
   701→        if key_input in sample and sample[key_input]:
   702→            prompt = self.template["prompt_input"].format(
   703→                instruction=sample[key_instruction], input=sample[key_input]
   704→            )
   705→        else:
   706→            prompt = self.template["prompt_no_input"].format(
   707→                instruction=sample[key_instruction]
   708→            )
   709→
   710→        messages = [
   711→            Message(
   712→                role="user",
   713→                content=prompt,
   714→                masked=not self.train_on_input,
   715→                eot=True,
   716→            ),
   717→            Message(
   718→                role="assistant",
   719→                content=sample[key_output],
   720→                masked=False,
   721→                eot=True,
   722→            ),
   723→        ]
   724→        return {"messages": messages}

text: Here’s what I did to reproduce the bug, implement the fix, and validate with tests. Per your instructions, I did not commit any changes. Summary of the issue - The transforms InputOutputToMessages and ShareGPTToMessages attempted to join image_dir and image_path using Path division syntax even when both were strings, causing TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for /: 'str' and 'str'. - Additionally, when image_path is a URL, it shouldn’t be joined with a local image_dir. Changes made 1) Reproduction tests - Added tests in tests/torchtune/data/test_messages_image_dir_normalization.py to cover: - Case A: image_dir as str, image_path as a relative string, for both InputOutputToMessages and ShareGPTToMessages. Assert that load_image receives Path(image_dir) / image_path. - Case B: image_dir as str, image_path as URL. Assert that load_image is called with the URL as-is (no joining). - Used unittest.mock.patch to patch torchtune.data._messages.load_image so we can capture its input and avoid actual I/O. 2) Code fixes in torchtune/data/_messages.py - InputOutputToMessages.__init__: - Updated type hint for image_dir to Optional[Union[str, Path]]. - Normalized to a Path if provided: self.image_dir = Path(image_dir) if image_dir is not None else None - InputOutputToMessages.__call__: - For string image_path, only join with image_dir when self.image_dir is not None and image_path does not start with "http://" or "https://". - After joining, pass the Path to load_image; if URL, pass the URL string unchanged. - ShareGPTToMessages.__init__: - Same normalization and type hint change as InputOutputToMessages. - ShareGPTToMessages.__call__: - Similarly guarded the join: if self.image_dir is not None and image_path is a str and not a URL, join with self.image_dir. Then call load_image with the result or URL. Notes: - Did not alter behavior when image_dir is None. - Ensured path joining results in a Path instance where applicable. Files touched - torchtune/data/_messages.py - tests/torchtune/data/test_messages_image_dir_normalization.py (new file) Test results - Initially, the new tests failed with the expected TypeError for the pre-fix code and incorrect joining for URL case. - After implementing the fixes: - New test file: 4 tests passed. - Full test suite: 623 passed, 93 skipped, 0 failed, 4 warnings. Acceptance criteria verification - Both InputOutputToMessages and ShareGPTToMessages accept image_dir as str or Path; joining with relative image_path works without TypeError. - URL image paths are not joined with image_dir and are passed directly to load_image. - Type annotations updated to Optional[Union[str, Path]] for image_dir in both classes. - New tests cover both classes and both cases (relative path and URL) and pass. - Existing tests continue to pass. If you’d like, I can create a commit with these changes and an appropriate message.
